idiom_name: typed template engines (EJS/Handlebars/Nunjucks with @types) behind Express/Fastify
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types around the same engines JavaScript uses: install EJS, Handlebars or Nunjucks with their @types packages, declare an interface for the view model and pass it to res.render, so the compiler checks the object handed to the template while the template's markers are still verified only at render time. Nunjucks (Jinja-like, inheritance and macros) and Handlebars (logic-less) are the usual choices behind Express/Fastify; for markup that lives in code, TypeScript's backtick template literals are the same construct as JavaScript's and escape nothing by themselves.
pitfalls: TypeScript checks the model object, not the template: a renamed marker in the .ejs file still compiles and renders empty.
Typings for these engines are shallow (the context is usually any/Record<string, unknown>), so the interface on the view model is discipline, not an enforced contract.
Development runners (ts-node/tsx) keep both the module cache and the template cache alive, so a corrected template can appear uncorrected until the process restarts.
